note: NOT new coverage — a numeric-precision fix to the already-ported _buildRiverSheet triangulation (citymap.js:7373-7614, river.json:591-677), closing the open RiverProbe vs tools/_probe_river.py count/area mismatch (C# 157559 verts/244112 tris/area 6569212 m^2 vs the reference 157547/244096/6569580). Root causes are TWO, independent, and were conflated before this fix: (1) COUNT (+12 verts/+16 tris): EarClip.Triangulate (citymap.js's THREE.ShapeUtils.triangulateShape equivalent, hand-rolled since Unity ships no earcut) is precision-sensitive near-degenerate is-ear/point-in-triangle cross-products, and citymap.js's own numbers (and _probe_river.py's) are always 64-bit JS/Python floats, never float32. The port stored ring coordinates in UnityEngine.Vector2 (32-bit) from JSON-parse time onward, losing bits BEFORE any triangulation math ran. Added per-ring 'RIVERP ringdbg' diagnostics to both RiverProbe.cs and _probe_river.py (merged-ring length + pre-subdivision triangle count per outer, printed before/after the 2 quad-subdivision passes) and diffed all 76 used rings: only ring i=6 (27 holes bridged into one 2399-point outer, the densest real ring) disagreed — pretris 1790 (C#) vs 1789 (Python) — every other ring matched exactly. First attempted fix (widen only the Cross/IsReflex/PointInTri arithmetic inside Triangulate to double, keeping Vector2 storage) did NOT change the result: the coordinates were already float32-rounded at parse time, so there was nothing left to recover by computing in double afterward. The real fix is RiverSheet.Vec2D, a new double-precision point struct that carries ring coordinates from ReadRing through Poly/RingRec/EarClip.MergeHoles/EarClip.Triangulate unrounded, converting to float only once, at Mesh/UV/Bank write time where float32 genuinely suffices. After the fix ring i=6 matches (pretris 1789, fverts 18917, ftris 28624, identical to Python) and so does the citywide total (157547/244096, exact). (2) AREA (368 m^2 gap, independent of the count bug): RiverSheet.BuildSheetAndBanks summed per-triangle shoelace area into a 32-bit `float` accumulator (`float area2`) over 244,112 terms; tools/_probe_river.py's `total_area = sum(...)` is a plain Python float, always 64-bit, with no such accumulation error. Changed the accumulator to `double`, casting to float only at SheetAreaM2's assignment. Verified together: after both fixes, `python3 tools/unity_port_check.py /tmp/river_js.txt <RiverProbe log>` reports PASS, 597 values matched, worst relative difference 2.794e-06 (float32 display rounding on an unrelated bed-height sample, not a regression), 0 js-only unmatched lines. WaterBodies.cs (a separate, shared consumer of RiverSheet.EarClip.Triangulate for lake contours, owned by another unit) was not touched: EarClip gained a Vector2-taking overload that forwards into the new double-precision one, so its existing call compiles and behaves unchanged (lake triangulation has no holes/bridging and was never shown to need the extra precision — this fix did not touch or re-verify WaterBodies' own numbers). RiverSheet's public surface (Build, HeightAt, LevelAt, MeasuredLevelAt, InRiverMask, RiverDepth, Mesh, Banks, all diagnostic counts) is unchanged; Vec2D and the new per-ring RingDebug list are additive.
